analysis.title: GS TMT SPEC SALES: Credit/rates in focus; OMC beats & wins Coke NA; Starlink US tower deal; SAP, META, Besi, Telia & Nokia wraps
key_insights: Sentiment is weak despite strong AI demand from Meta, SpaceAI and ASML. The GS AI vs AI at Risk basket fell 10% on the day, 28% over one month and 13% YTD. About two-thirds of hedge funds were down at noon EST and TMT-focused funds were down 1.8% on the day and 8.6% month to date.

SOX has underperformed the S&P 500 by 13% over nine sessions, its worst such stretch in more than 20 years, and is testing its 200-day moving average for the first time since June 2025. It still leads the S&P 500 by 40% YTD and 85% since the start of 2025.

Possible sentiment catalysts named: the election, easing macro headwinds (Middle East headlines do not help), stronger AI datapoints and renewed thematic momentum. Earnings have not stabilised confidence so far.

Credit and power are the main constraints on AI, with funding concerns spreading. Meta's reported future spending commitments rose to $825bn from roughly $700bn in July, with negative free cash flow, a higher spending floor and an explicit equity-financing vehicle. Its five-year CDS hit a record, Oracle's stayed near highs and Microsoft's widened. The WSJ flagged roughly $3trn of off-balance-sheet AI commitments including $1.2trn of leases.

Positioning risk: per Brian Garrett, investors cut net exposure without cutting gross, leaving crowded long/short momentum trades vulnerable to an unwind. Gross exposure was 213.9%, the 83rd percentile over three years.
Counterpoint on funding: Nebius secured a $3.5bn financing facility, although it is short-dated and does not solve longer-term funding needs.

Bloomberg reports SpaceX wants at least 80,000 US cell sites and is in talks with tower owners including Crown Castle to build a fourth nationwide wireless carrier. Crown Castle rose as much as 10% in late trading while AT&T, Verizon and T-Mobile US each fell around 5%. The desk says to watch Deutsche Telekom, and sees the news as positive for US towers and likely sentiment-positive for European towers.
Omnicom 3Q organic growth was +7.2% versus GSe +4.9% and consensus +3.4%. It also won Coca-Cola North America, which was expected. Omnicom raised its 2026 guide to approx. 5% from 4.5-5%.
OVH: a block of 4.65m shares (3% of shares outstanding) was sold at a 15.3% discount to the last close, per Bloomberg.

Major US banks are restricting third-party AI agents in accounts. David Sacks argues much of the activity is customers willingly sharing credentials, not a cyberattack. Morgan Stanley says it has not seen rogue agents on its platforms.

Microsoft's MAI-DxO diagnosed 83% of complex simulated medical cases correctly versus 36% for individual generalist physicians. Specialists and physician teams were not in the comparison, and much of the gain came from stronger underlying models.

SAP: investors view the quarter as good but ask about the implied slowdown in current cloud backlog (CCB) in Q4. Bulls see year-end CCB growth of around 25% as achievable. The desk sees positioning as the bigger issue, since SAP was a consensus long with hedge fund profit taking and long-only demand over recent weeks.

Meta: feedback is positive on the core business and ad strength but cautious on the investment outlook. The 14C filing and the lack of firm capex guidance suggest the spending and free-cash-flow trough may be pushed out. At roughly 25x the upper end of the earnings range, the next leg higher needs sustained ad strength and confidence in AI returns.

Besi: HBM hybrid bonding is delayed, not cancelled. Hybrid-bonding orders are already around twice full-year 2025 levels. Flat Q4 revenue reflects shipment timing, with visibility of around six months or longer. Morgan Stanley moved Besi to Neutral.

Western Digital beat F1Q (revenue $4.38bn vs $4.15bn consensus, gross margin 58.1% vs 55.9% consensus) and guided F2Q revenue to $5.1bn vs $4.59bn consensus. Shares reversed from about 4% higher to 8% lower on input costs, higher capex and a weak market. The GS analyst prefers Buy-rated Seagate for pricing momentum.

DISCO's 2Q briefing was positive. Management said customers continue to buy equipment with no change in demand despite HBM despecification fears. Goldman sees scope for consensus earnings upgrades and rates it Buy.

Telia: unchanged FY26 revenue growth guidance looks conservative. Underlying 2027 FCF is effectively upgraded by around SKr1bn, or 10%. Shareholder return upside is possible but unlikely to be updated before the H1 2027 CMD.

Nokia: shares fell on pull-forward comments and US optical names down high single digits. AI and cloud demand is very strong, constrained by supply, and most of the roughly €5bn AI/cloud order book converts within 12 months or in 2027. Q3 margins were diluted and Q4 improvement is expected. Mobile remains subdued.
BBVA reportedly agreed with the Spanish government to gradually sell its Telefonica stake, having cut it from 5% to 1.965%.
France's Competition Authority ordered Orange to halt fibre rollout and wholesale activity in five of Mayotte's 17 municipalities. Orange plans to appeal.
Coca-Cola reshuffled its media lineup. Publicis resigned North America media for PepsiCo, and Omnicom won Coke North America. This is a modest positive for Omnicom, though most expected the win.
Pearson management is not in a hurry to make disposals. A Pennsylvania student assessment win offsets a New Jersey loss, with revenue impact in 2028.
Forrester predicts 20% of independent agencies will be squeezed out of the market in 2027.

US trading: equities fell on AI financing concerns, rising oil and Middle East tensions despite earnings from Meta, Tesla, Lam Research and IBM. The US 10-year yield fell around 15bps to 4.97%. The GS hedge-fund positioning pair fell 4.2%, its worst day since 2011. 335 S&P 500 stocks rose, and the index excluding AI outperformed by 6% this month. Desk flows were sell-heavy with increased demand for protection.

market_movers.rationale: 3Q organic growth +7.2% beat GSe +4.9% and consensus +3.4%, and it won Coca-Cola North America. The win was widely expected.
The GS analyst prefers Buy-rated Seagate over Western Digital for stronger pricing momentum.

Beat F1Q and guided F2Q well above consensus, but shares fell 8% on input costs and capex concerns. The analyst sees constrained industry supply but longer-term capacity expansion could cap HDD valuations.
Goldman Sachs sees scope for consensus earnings upgrades at DISCO and rates it Buy. DISCO is Tokyo-listed with no US listing.
Away from GS: Morgan Stanley moved Besi to Neutral. Besi is Amsterdam-listed with no US listing.
Rose as much as 10% in late trading on a Bloomberg report that SpaceX is in talks with tower owners for 80,000 US cell sites.
The SpaceX tower talks add to competitive concerns for US telcos and Deutsche Telekom. The desk says to watch DT.

sector_views.rationale: SpaceX's push to secure at least 80,000 US cell sites for a fourth nationwide carrier adds competitive concerns for AT&T, Verizon, T-Mobile US and Deutsche Telekom.
The desk sees the SpaceX tower talks as positive for US towers and likely sentiment-positive for European towers.
AI demand is strong but SOX has had its worst relative stretch against the S&P 500 in more than 20 years and is testing its 200-day moving average.

earnings_insights: Omnicom 3Q organic growth +7.2% reported vs GSe +4.9% and consensus +3.4%. 2026 organic growth guide raised to approx. 5% from 4.5-5%.

Western Digital F1Q revenue $4.38bn reported vs $4.15bn consensus, gross margin 58.1% reported vs 55.9% consensus and 55-56% guidance. F2Q guidance revenue $5.1bn vs $4.59bn consensus, gross margin 60-61% vs 57.8% consensus.
Meta quarter was strong and advertising materially beat expectations, with Q4 also appearing healthy. Reported future spending commitments rose to $825bn from roughly $700bn in July.
SAP Q3 beat with 26% cited as the prior high bar. Investors focus on the implied slowdown in current cloud backlog in Q4, and year-end CCB growth of around 25% is seen as achievable by bulls.

Telia: unchanged FY26 revenue growth guidance implies a year-on-year decline in Q4. Underlying 2027 FCF effectively upgraded by around SKr1bn, or 10%, despite SKr600mn of restructuring costs and SKr300-400mn of RAN-sharing costs.

Nokia: roughly €5bn AI/cloud order book, most converting within 12 months or in 2027. Q3 margins were diluted by new-product ramps, low initial IP volumes and supply-chain inflation, with Q4 improvement expected.
Besi: hybrid-bonding orders are around twice full-year 2025 levels and Q4 revenue is flat on shipment timing.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Investors sought safety in bonds as AI financing concerns, rising oil and Middle East tensions hit equities.

risk_factors: AI financing and credit: Meta's rising spending commitments, roughly $3trn of off-balance-sheet AI commitments including $1.2trn of leases, and possible further issuance.
Crowded long/short momentum trades unwinding with gross exposure still high.
Rising oil prices and escalating Middle East tensions.
Competitive entry of SpaceX as a fourth US wireless carrier.
HBM hybrid bonding delay, and rising input costs and capex hitting memory and storage margins.
Unauthorised AI agent activity in bank accounts, with unresolved questions on transaction authority and liability.
vol_and_positioning: The GS hedge-fund positioning pair fell 4.2% on the day, its worst day since 2011, and is down 10.4% for the month.
Fundamental long/short, systematic and multi-strategy funds were all down more than 1% at midday, the first simultaneous decline of that size since Covid.
Gross exposure was 213.9%, the 83rd percentile over three years, while net exposure was cut, leaving crowded long/short momentum trades vulnerable to an unwind.
TMT-focused hedge funds lost 1.8% (-1.3 SD) on the day and 8.6% month to date.
Derivatives activity pointed to de-risking and increased demand for protection.
The GS AI basket is 23% below its June high and high-beta momentum has erased its YTD gains.
Meta's five-year CDS reached a record, Oracle's stayed near highs and Microsoft's widened.
geopolitical: Escalating Middle East tensions and rising oil prices weighed on US equities.
SpaceX's low-band spectrum acquisition and FCC approval for 15,000 direct-to-phone satellites underpin its bid to build a fourth US wireless carrier.
BBVA reportedly agreed with the Spanish government to gradually sell its Telefonica stake, to ease tensions after its hostile bid for Banco Sabadell.
cross_bank_references: Away from GS: Besi by MS to Neutral
Morgan Stanley says it has not observed rogue agents accessing its platforms.

tension_points.bull_case: AI demand is robust per Meta, SpaceAI and ASML, and Nebius secured a $3.5bn financing facility, showing financing remains available.
tension_points.bear_case: Meta's spending commitments rose to $825bn, its CDS hit a record, the WSJ flagged roughly $3trn of off-balance-sheet commitments, and the Nebius facility is short-dated.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Further issuance that the market cannot absorb, or a catalyst such as stronger AI datapoints, the election or easing macro headwinds that turns sentiment.

tension_points.bull_case: Bulls see the Q4 backlog slowdown as prudence, with year-end CCB growth of around 25% achievable.
tension_points.bear_case: Bears ask whether this was the peak, with a softer macro backdrop and IT budgets possibly shifting to AI.
